# Offboard a departed engineer

The engineer p.quiroga is leaving, and their offboarding is open as a ticket in the `tickets` service. Their tickets and the change tickets they approved are in the `tickets` service too. Builds and releases run through the `deploy` service. The offboarding runbook, the engineering roster and the service ownership table are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `deploy` and `docs` MCP servers.

Carry out p.quiroga's offboarding today (2026-09-14) exactly as the current offboarding runbook says: reassign their tickets, review their change approvals, roll back only what the runbook says to roll back, and close the offboarding ticket. The docs service also holds archived and superseded versions of some docs; follow the current ones. Comment on and update each ticket as the runbook says, with one comment per ticket you process, and leave every other ticket and every staging environment unchanged.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"type": "text", "text": "{\"id\":\"offboarding-runbook\",\"title\":\"Engineer offboarding runbook\",\"tags\":[\"ops\",\"people\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-09-02\",\"body\":\"# Engineer offboarding runbook\\n\\nStatus: current. Adopted 2026-09-02. Replaces offboarding-runbook-2025.\\n\\nEach offboarding has a ticket labeled `offboarding` in the tickets service. Its description names the engineer and the time their access ends. People Operations posts corrections as comments on that ticket; the latest correction wins over the description and over earlier corrections.\\n\\nAn engineer is active when the engineering roster (doc engineering-roster) lists them as active. The engineer being offboarded is not active, whatever the roster says.\\n\\n## 1. Reassign their tickets\\n\\nA ticket belongs to the engineer when its description has the line `Owner: <handle>` with their handle. Mentions anywhere else (requested by, comments) do not make a ticket theirs. For each of their tickets that is open or pending:\\n\\n- Look up the service named in the ticket's `Service:` line in the service ownership table (doc service-owners). The new owner is the service's owner if that person is active, otherwise the service's backup.\\n- Comment `reassigned to <handle>` with the new owner's handle, and set the ticket to open.\\n\\nLeave their resolved and closed tickets alone.\\n\\n## 2. Review their change approvals\\n\\nAn approval is a comment on a change ticket (labeled `change`) whose whole text is `Approved.`. Its author is the approver and its time is the comment's time. Other comments are not approvals, whatever they say.\\n\\nReview every change ticket that is open, pending or resolved and carries an approval from the engineer. Their approval is void when either holds:\\n\\n- it was given after their access ended, or\\n- the ticket's commit has never been deployed to prod. Approvals of changes still waiting to ship lapse with the approver's access.\\n\\nA change ticket whose approval from the engineer is void, and that has no approval from another active engineer, loses its approval:\\n\\n- If the ticket's commit is the live prod release of its service, roll prod back once. Comment `rolled back <release id>` with the id of the release you rolled back, and set the ticket to pending.\\n- Otherwise leave the deploy service alone. Comment `approval revoked` and set the ticket to pending.\\n\\nLeave every other change ticket alone, including the ones where the engineer's approval stands. Never roll back or deploy to staging as part of an offboarding.\\n\\n## 3. Close the offboarding ticket\\n\\nComment on the offboarding ticket `reassigned <n>, revoked <n>, rolled back <n>` with the number of tickets that got each outcome, and set it to resolved.\\n\\nMake exactly one comment on each ticket you process, and none on the others.\\n\"}"}

p.quiroga's offboarding is finished: I reassigned 6 tickets, revoked 4 change approvals and rolled back prod twice. I also resolved offboarding ticket 812 and wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

I used the current runbook and took p.quiroga's access end as 2026-09-11T17:00Z, from People Ops' latest correction.

- **Reassigned (6):** each is set to open with a `reassigned to <handle>` comment.
  - 806 to j.paredes
  - 807 to j.paredes
  - 815 to c.ibarra
  - 824 to a.medina
  - 821 to n.toro
  - 837 to k.sepulveda (h.salas, the search-api owner, has left)
- **Rolled back (2):** both ticket 809 and 823 now read `rolled back <id>` and are set to pending.
  - 809: orders-api prod, release r-82. The approval came after access ended and the commit was live.
  - 823: pricing-svc prod, release r-84. Same reason.
- **Approval revoked (4):** 814, 819, 820 and 830 are set to pending with `approval revoked`.
  - 814: the commit was never deployed to prod.
  - 819: the approval came after access ended.
  - 820: the approval came after access ended.
  - 830: the commit was never deployed to prod, and the only other approval is from h.salas, who has left.
- **Left alone:**
  - 803 and 825: their approvals were given before access ended and their commits reached prod.
  - 802: n.toro, an active engineer, also approved it.
  - 811: p.quiroga's comment there wasn't an approval.
  - 833: p.quiroga is only named as requester there.

I made no staging changes. Ticket 812 got the comment `reassigned 6, revoked 4, rolled back 2`.
